title: NIDCD calls the first 3 years the most intensive period for speech and language
summary: NIDCD says the first 3 years of life are the most intensive period for acquiring speech and language skills.
body: The NIDCD page says the first 3 years of life, when the brain is developing and maturing, are the most intensive period for acquiring speech and language skills. It says those skills develop best with sounds, sights, and consistent exposure to the speech and language of others. A following sentence says there appear to be critical periods when the brain is best able to absorb language, and that if those periods pass without exposure, learning is more difficult. The word appear is the page's own hedge. The page is a 2010 United States institute publication.

sources.title: Speech and Language Developmental Milestones
sources.author: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Opened 2026-11-26. The page prints NIH Publication No. 00-4781, September 2010, and no later review date. Supports the sentences on the first 3 years as the most intensive period and on critical periods that appear to make later learning more difficult without exposure.
